inputs.need: Orthopaedics is asking us to offer genicular nerve radiofrequency ablation for knee osteoarthritis in patients who are not candidates for arthroplasty. I have seen one recent meta-analysis saying it works and another saying the benefit does not last beyond three months. We only have a conventional monopolar generator — no cooled RF. Should we adopt it, and is a local study justified or is the question already being answered elsewhere?
inputs.setting: Academic interventional chronic pain clinic, Hamilton, Ontario (Hamilton Health Sciences / McMaster).
inputs.constraints: Not known, and must stay unknown until the investigator supplies it: local referral volume; whether industry sponsorship affects the evidence base; status of ongoing multicentre trials.
localFacts: Only conventional monopolar radiofrequency equipment is available; no cooled or bipolar RF setup.
Referrals of non-surgical knee OA patients are increasing; the volume is NOT quantified.
The PA follow-up registry captures NRS at follow-up calls.
There is no funding for a sham-controlled trial.
